**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

**What I found.** The sole grant clause (para 2, p0002) licenses the Auction Platform to "Customer" alone on a "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, **revocable**" basis. Para 8(a) (p0025) compounds this by prohibiting any third-party access to the Service without Kubient's prior written approval, so there is no notice-based path to bring AP affiliates or contractors under the licence.

**Why it fails the fallback.** The fallback requires at minimum that affiliates be covered on written notice and that the licence transfer to an M&A successor. The assignment clause (p0072) does permit assignment to an affiliate or a merger/stock-sale successor without consent, which satisfies the transferability limb. But affiliates and contractors remain excluded from the grant with only a Kubient-consent gate, and the licence is revocable at Kubient's discretion independent of the para 4 termination machinery — that is squarely the walk-away formulation.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** A single edit to p0002:
- adds "its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf" to the grantees;
- deletes "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable";
- ties revocation to expiration or termination under para 4 and confirms transfer to a successor under the existing assignment provisions.

I flagged this at the preferred position rather than the fallback because the at-will revocability is the more serious defect and cannot be fixed by an affiliate-notice mechanic alone. The comment offers affiliate-coverage-on-written-notice as a fallback if Kubient resists.

One drafting note I did **not** flag, since it is outside this rule: para 4(c)(ii) (p0021) refers to "the license granted under section 3," but the grant is in section 2 — worth correcting for consistency, particularly if the revocability edit above is accepted.
